data.name: Abel
data.gender_notes: Abel is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Abel is derived from the Hebrew word 'hebel', which means 'breath' or 'vapor'. In the Bible, Abel is the name of the second son of Adam and Eve. He is known for offering the first acceptable sacrifice to God, consisting of the firstlings of his flock and their fat. Unfortunately, Abel's brother Cain, who was jealous of Abel's favor with God, murdered him.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the fleeting nature of earthly possessions and worldly success, reminding us to focus on our spiritual connection with God.
data.etymology: Abel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Breath.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Abel total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Abel has been used in various English-speaking cultures since ancient times. It has been popularized by figures in different fields, including the poet and statesman Lord George Gordon Byron and the American baseball player Abel James "Abie" Habib.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Bible, Abel is regarded as a symbol of faithfulness and devotion to God. He is remembered for offering the first acceptable sacrifice to God, which shows his obedience and his desire to please God. Unfortunately, his life was ended prematurely by his brother Cain's jealousy and hatred, reflecting the themes of sin, jealousy, and the value of righteousness in the face of adversity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Abel: The name Abel in the Bible symbolizes innocence and righteousness. He was the second son of Adam and Eve, and the first human offering to God. His sacrifice was accepted, representing a life lived in harmony with divine will.

biblical_reference.note: The story of Cain and Abel appears in the book of Genesis, chapters 4:1-16.

historical_references.context: Abel is the name of the second son of Adam and Eve. He is the brother of Cain. Abel kept flocks, while Cain was a tiller of the ground. When they brought offerings to God, Abel's offering was accepted, but Cain's was not. In jealousy, Cain killed Abel.

historical_references.context: Saint Abel is one of the Seven Sleepers of Ephesus. According to legend, a pagan priest buried seven Christian youths in a cave to protect them from persecution during the Roman Emperor Decius' reign. The youths slept for 170 years until they were awakened by a bishop. Saint Abel and his companions continued to live as hermits and were later venerated as saints.
